clue.text: Man and goddess in conflict with flier

indicators.note: 'in conflict' reads as the man and goddess placed inside the word for conflict

parts.note: conflict means war
a man is a he
Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and mischief

explanation.surface: A man and a goddess are locked in combat with some kind of airman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflict' gives the outer word, as 'in conflict' means at war; Ate is a less familiar goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird, so a flier in crossword terms.

clue.text: A spot of shuteye?

parts.note: read not as a brief nap but as a literal spot, a small swelling, on an eye that shuts

explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a spot where the eye closes.

clue.text: Ring twice for sin with great little woman

parts.note: great means big
Amy is the youngest March sister in Alcott's novel Little Women

explanation.surface: Someone is told to ring the doorbell twice to commit a sin with a grand little lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: two wedding rings at once is the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy is marrying a second spouse while still married, so taking a wedding ring twice, a sin and crime.

clue.text: One supports runner with a long drink of water

definitions.meaning: a tall garden stake holds up a climbing runner-bean plant
slang for a very tall, thin person

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the stake for climbing beans and, figuratively, a lanky person.

clue.text: Where St Catherine turned to driving

definitions.meaning: Saint Catherine of Alexandria was condemned to be broken on a spiked wheel
in control of a vehicle, holding the steering

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means steering a car, and literally where the martyr was bound on the Catherine wheel.

clue.text: Overcoat thus keeping body of unionists cold

indicators.note: one word keeping others means holding them inside it

parts.note: thus means so
the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the UK federation of trade unions
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A coat is described as holding a group of trade unionists out in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcoat' is not a garment but a coating over a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is fine plaster applied as an outer coating over building walls.

clue.text: Our representatives shattered it, the fools!

indicators.note: to fool is to trick or befuddle, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry citizen complains that parliamentarians have wrecked something, idiots that they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: 'fools' rearranges SHATTERED IT THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The commons, the ordinary people represented in parliament, were historically called the third order of the realm.

clue.text: Want what shall have no dominion outside the king

indicators.note: the first piece stands outside, around, the royal letter

parts.note: Dylan Thomas's poem 'And death shall have no dominion' names this
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone wishes for whatever will lack power beyond the monarch's reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Dylan Thomas (after Romans 6:9): 'And death shall have no dominion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack, the noun sense of want.

clue.text: See 7
Put off work on the Met Office roof?

definitions.meaning: to postpone or defer an offer

definitions.text: work on the Met Office roof?
definitions.meaning: literally checking the rainfall, as a weather observer on the forecaster's roof would

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to decline now but promise to accept later, so to defer.

clue.text: See 10
A Dickensian Berty Wooster curtailed Tod Slaughter!

indicators.note: slaughter as massacre, so the letters are hacked about into a new order
a word curtailed has its tail, the last letter, cut off

explanation.surface: Wodehouse's hero, cut short, is set beside the old melodrama actor Tod Slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the final R of BERTY WOOSTER; 'Slaughter' then mixes BERTYWOOSTE with TOD. Tod Slaughter looks like a name but splits into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Betsey Trotwood is David Copperfield's formidable great-aunt in Dickens's novel, so a Dickensian character.

clue.text: Numbers air essential to this voyager

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are taken as the essence from which the traveller is formed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller under the sea is said to need certain quantities of air.
explanation.walkthrough: Air is indeed essential to an undersea voyager; the letters of NUMBERS AIR rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A submariner is a crew member of a submarine, a voyager beneath the sea.

clue.text: See 12
With which bridge players stick together?

definitions.text: With which bridge players stick together?

parts.words: With which bridge players stick together?
parts.note: a bridge game is played in ..., so the card players' glue is jokingly named after that unit of play

explanation.definitionFit: Rubber cement is a latex adhesive, and a rubber is a set of games in bridge.

clue.text: Recording giant's run-in, say, with agent

parts.note: EMI is the British record company, here with its possessive

indicators.note: 'run-in' read as run placed in the following word

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A record label's quarrel, for example, is resolved with a business agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run-in' looks like a quarrel, but 'in' puts R inside SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is someone sent on a mission as a representative, an agent.

clue.text: See 15
With which Indian chefs make an entrance: is it holding up?

indicators.note: one piece holding another contains it
in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
an entrance is a door

explanation.surface: Indian cooks sweep in through the doorway, and someone asks whether a structure is staying up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT into TI, which then holds AN + DOOR; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori dishes are cooked by Indian chefs in a tandoor, a clay oven.

clue.text: "Tell it not in ____" with two articles about her

indicators.note: the two articles are placed about, that is around, the missing word

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, taken twice
David's lament in 2 Samuel: 'Tell it not in Gath', the Philistine city

explanation.surface: A biblical quotation with a gap is completed by surrounding a word with two little words.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled from the Bible: 'Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon.'
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a woman's name, so a 'her' in the clue's terms.

clue.text: Glad inflation's off course

indicators.note: off as gone wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of inflation plus the s of the possessive, used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that rising prices have veered away from their path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off course' looks like one phrase, but 'off' is the anagram signal and 'course' the definition, as in a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating island is a dessert of poached meringue on custard, a pudding course.

clue.text: Deadlock being Napier's preserve?

explanation.definitionFit: A log jam is a blockage of floating timber, and figuratively a standstill.

clue.text: See 20
Pacific island could be nicer

indicators.note: the word nicer could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A tropical island in the Pacific might be even pleasanter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' looks like the ocean, but it is the adjective meaning peaceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Irenic means peaceful or conciliatory, the same sense as pacific.

clue.text: Shearer's backward pass thus contrarily went to his goal: a mistake

indicators.note: a mistake garbles things, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Footballer Alan Shearer's back-pass went into his own net by error.
explanation.walkthrough: Shearer looks like the England striker, but is a sheep shearer cutting the wrong way through the fleece; 'mistake' rearranges WENT TO HIS GOAL A.
explanation.definitionFit: Running counter to the natural lie of the fleece means acting contrarily, like going against the grain.

clue.text: See 23
Wimbledon commoners ignoring the foreign child care unit

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letters named after it

parts.note: the Wombles are furry creatures of a British children's TV series who live on Wimbledon Common in London
les is French for the

explanation.surface: Residents of a London common pay no heed to a foreign nursery facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child care unit' is not a crèche but where an unborn child is cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: The womb shelters and nourishes the developing child before birth, a cryptic care unit.

clue.text: Vocation of one tending to go out East

indicators.note: the first piece is to go outside the next, so it wraps around it

parts.note: a carer is one who tends the sick

explanation.surface: Someone with a nursing calling is inclined to emigrate eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a person's chosen profession or calling, a vocation.

clue.text: The Bible that is second to scripture in Scotland

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
a mo is a moment, a second
RE is religious education, school scripture lessons

explanation.surface: A claim that a particular Bible ranks just behind scripture itself north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the definition is minimal, just saying where the place is.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviemore is a resort town in the Scottish Highlands, a place found in Scotland.
